slides.title: Uncovering Salience-Driven Dynamics in Consumer Confidence with Generative Social Simulation
slides.tldr: GENERATIVE SOCIAL SIMULATION FOR CONSUMER CONFIDENCE
slides.highlight: This work introduces ConsumerSim, a generative framework that reconstructs Consumer Confidence Index dynamics using synthetic populations and behavioral responses, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: ConsumerSim reconstructs Consumer Confidence Index dynamics as a salience-driven response process between heterogeneous agents and environments.
card.key_idea: A generative framework using microdata-calibrated synthetic populations, situational signal fields, and behavioral inertia alignment to simulate how specific demographic groups respond to salient economic shocks.
card.evaluation: Evaluated against U.S., EU27, and Japan CCI series; outperformed 14 baselines (MAE/RMSE) and improved short-horizon housing activity predictions.
card.limitation: Relies on external signal quality, uses generative agents as imperfect cognitive proxies, and lacks full local population substrates for non-U.S. regions.

slides.title: A Role-Based Multi-Agent Model for Climate Adaptation Deliberation Across Living Labs
slides.tldr: MULTI-LEVEL AGENT-BASED ARCHITECTURE FOR CLIMATE GOVERNANCE
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a modular multi-agent architecture integrating cognitive decision models and institutional behavior, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent-based impact analysis.

card.one_liner: A configurable multi-agent model for simulating climate adaptation deliberations across different Living Lab settings.
card.key_idea: A role-based architecture separating fixed behavioral mechanisms from externalized context-specific inputs, allowing agents to perform multiple roles (Expert, Disseminator, Positioning Agent, Decision-Maker) across four phases.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper reports a design contribution rather than a completed validation study.
card.limitation: The model currently lacks empirical validation and testing across actual Living Labs.

slides.title: When May I Help You? On The Effect of Proactivity on Group Human-Robot Collaboration
slides.highlight: This study examines how proactive versus reactive robot initiative affects group coordination and performance, contributing to HyECHO's focus on addressee modeling and engagement in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: Robot proactivity in group collaboration is heavily influenced by users' prior experience and personality traits.
card.key_idea: Compared a reactive robot (responds only when addressed) against a proactive one (listens continuously, initiates interaction) using an LLM-powered humanoid in a collaborative escape room.
card.evaluation: 56 participants (28 pairs) evaluated via puzzle-solving time, success rates, and Godspeed/RoSAS scales. Results show proactive models increase interaction frequency but vary by user profile.
card.limitation: Small sample size for certain subgroups (e.g., LLM-inexperienced) and potential selection bias in late-stage puzzle solving times.

slides.title: Understanding LLM Intervention Explanations in Multi-Party Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This research examines how LLM-based orchestrators justify intervention decisions in multi-party human-robot interactions, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: LLM-driven robots in multi-party settings primarily act as facilitators, prioritizing agreement, participation balance, and fairness.
card.key_idea: An LLM orchestrator manages two robots (mover and opposer) in human groups, generating textual justifications for its real-time intervention decisions to analyze behavioral patterns.
card.evaluation: Thematic analysis of 610 explanations from 24 groups (66 students) using a between-subjects study with homogeneous and heterogeneous robot roles.
card.limitation: Did not evaluate if explanations improved user-perceived transparency or link robot behaviors to objective task success rates.

slides.title: SkillSpotter: Pose-Aware Multi-View Skilled Action Detection and Grading in Ego-Exo Videos
slides.tldr: MULTI-VIEW SKILLED ACTION DETECTION AND GRADING
slides.highlight: SkillSpotter utilizes a pose-aware multi-view architecture to detect and grade skilled actions in ego-exo videos, supporting the MOSAIC goal of estimating human proficiency through ego-exo views and body kinematics.

card.one_liner: SkillSpotter jointly detects and grades skilled actions in ego-exo videos using pose-aware multi-view architecture.
card.key_idea: Combines adaptive temporal suppression for varying action density, gated 3D body pose fusion, and bidirectional cross-view attention to integrate egocentric and exocentric visual streams.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Ego-Exo4D and HoloAssist against seven TAD baselines; improved class-specific mAP from 12.40 to 21.82 and balanced accuracy to 60.40%.
card.limitation: Struggles with fine-grained hand-object interactions in scenarios like cooking and music, where body-pose cues are insufficient.

slides.title: UBTech launches lifelike humanoid robots built for companionship in China
slides.highlight: The launch of lifelike humanoid robots for companionship is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Who Plays Which Role When? Communication Role Dynamics for Peer Recognition and Team Performance Prediction
slides.tldr: COMMUNICATION ROLE DYNAMICS FOR TEAM PERFORMANCE
slides.highlight: This work operationalizes a taxonomy of communication roles to characterize role dynamics and predict team performance, contributing to HyECHO's focus on modeling hybrid team states and engagement.

card.one_liner: Theory-grounded communication roles predicted by LLMs outperform lexical and conversational baselines in predicting team performance.
card.key_idea: Operationalized a taxonomy of eight communicative roles using LLMs to annotate longitudinal Slack data, analyzing role dynamics and their predictive power for peer recognition.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a student Slack corpus and DeliData using ROC-AUC; compared against BoW, conversational features, and zero-shot LLM baselines.
card.limitation: Primary data from a single CS course; potential selection bias from consenting students and reliance on proprietary LLM reasoning models.

slides.title: LLM-Powered Interactive Robotic Action Synthesis from Multimodal Speech, Gestures, and Music
slides.highlight: This framework uses LLMs to synthesize robotic actions from speech, gestures, and music, supporting the RwB goal of creating more fluid and context-aware human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A framework using LLMs to synthesize quadruped robot actions from speech, hand gestures, and music beats.
card.key_idea: Multimodal inputs (Whisper ASR, gesture recognition, beat detection) are formatted into prompts for an LLM, which maps them to a pre-vetted robotic action space.
card.evaluation: Validated on a Unitree Go2 quadruped robot using Qwen3:0.6b; demonstrated successful execution of a handstand triggered by gestures and music.
card.limitation: Currently relies on a limited, predefined action space and requires further optimization for real-time responsiveness.

slides.title: Triadic Werewolf: A Jester Role for Multi-Hop Theory of Mind in LLMs
slides.highlight: This research introduces a triadic incentive structure in the Werewolf game to evaluate multi-hop theory of mind and multi-agent reasoning in LLMs, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on inferring partner intent.

card.one_liner: A new triadic Werewolf benchmark reveals LLMs struggle with multi-hop Theory of Mind reasoning.
card.key_idea: Introducing a Jester role with inverted utility breaks simple 'suspicion' heuristics, requiring models to reason across three competing faction goals to win.
card.evaluation: 60 games using GPT-4.1, DeepSeek-V3.1, and Llama-3.3-70B; measured via win-rates, voting dynamics, and a Jester self-learning loop. Results show high Jester win-rates.
card.limitation: Small sample size (10 games per cell) leads to wide confidence intervals; only tested in English.

slides.title: Reference-Based Prosody and Rhythm Evaluation for Spoken Dialogue Systems
slides.highlight: This work introduces a percentile-based evaluation protocol for conversational prosody and rhythm, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: A reference-based evaluation protocol for assessing prosody and rhythm plausibility in spoken dialogue systems.
card.key_idea: Uses 4,000+ hours of dyadic conversation to create matched reference strata (by sex, age, arousal, dominance) for percentile-based behavioral plausibility checks of S2S outputs.
card.evaluation: Tested on held-out human rows; matched references correctly flagged ~10% of samples, whereas pooled references over-flagged state-conditioned expressivity and rhythm.
card.limitation: Based on a single English corpus; uses model-predicted traits instead of ground-truth metadata; does not map to perceptual naturalness.

slides.title: Vision-Language Models for Deployable Social Robot Navigation: Bridging Semantic Reasoning and Low-Level Control
slides.highlight: This survey explores integrating Vision-Language Models with low-level control to achieve socially compliant robot navigation, supporting RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A survey proposing a hierarchical framework to bridge high-level VLM semantic reasoning with low-level robot control.
card.key_idea: Organizes VLM-based social navigation into three components: high-level reasoning, a bridging module for translating semantics into planner-facing quantities, and low-level planning for safe, socially compliant execution.
card.evaluation: Reviews representative datasets and evaluation platforms for social robot navigation; focuses on human-centered outcomes like comfort, safety, and legibility.
card.limitation: High computational cost and inference latency of VLMs hinder real-time deployment on resource-constrained mobile robots.

slides.title: Reinforcement Learning with Metacognitive Feedback Elicits Faithful Uncertainty Expression in LLMs
slides.highlight: This work introduces reinforcement learning with metacognitive feedback (RLMF) to improve how LLMs monitor and express their own uncertainty. This is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and self-correction via meta-cognition.

card.one_liner: RLMF improves LLM trustworthiness by aligning expressed uncertainty with intrinsic confidence using metacognitive feedback.
card.key_idea: Reinforcement Learning with Metacognitive Feedback (RLMF) scales learning advantages based on a model's self-judgment accuracy, paired with metacognitive data selection and a numerical-to-linguistic rewriting stage.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 10 datasets using Llama3.1 and Qwen3; measured via cMFG*, accuracy, and human preference. RLMF outperformed standard RL by up to 63%.
card.limitation: Improved metacognitive capabilities are not substitutes for verification; autonomous or self-directed behaviors may require increased oversight.

slides.title: SenseWalk: Agent-Based Semantic Trajectory Simulation Powered by Large Language Models in Zoned Environments
slides.highlight: SenseWalk uses LLM-powered agents and the social force model to simulate human movement patterns and semantic trajectories, aligning with MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: SenseWalk is an interactive system using LLM-powered agents to simulate semantic trajectories in zoned environments.
card.key_idea: Combines LLMs for high-level semantic planning and reasoning with a social force model to ensure physically plausible, collision-free pedestrian movement.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via quantitative experiments across four real-world venue datasets using physical and semantic loss metrics, plus a 12-person user study.

slides.title: REPAIR-Bench: A Benchmark for Robot Error Perception And Interaction Recovery
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR ROBOT FAILURE PERCEPTION AND RECOVERY
slides.highlight: This benchmark introduces a framework for evaluating how users perceive robot failures and predicting preferred recovery strategies, supporting the development of trustworthy human-robot interaction for RwB.

card.one_liner: REPAIR-Bench is a multimodal benchmark for detecting, classifying, and predicting recovery strategies for robot failures.
card.key_idea: It uses a Hierarchical Recurrent Neural Network (HRNN) for visual failure detection/classification and QLoRA-tuned Small Language Models (SLMs) to predict user-preferred recovery strategies from transcripts.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 184 interaction trials using F1-scores, localization error (MAE), and Hit@k. HRNN achieved 0.80 strict F1; Mistral-7B QLoRA reached Hit@5 of 0.76.
card.limitation: Small sample size (184) for recovery prediction and reliance on a predefined set of recovery strategies.

slides.title: Theory of Mind and Persuasion Beyond Conversation: Assessing the Capacity of LLMs to Induce Belief States via Planning and Action
slides.highlight: This research introduces NCP-ExploreToM to evaluate an agent's ability to induce belief states through actions rather than conversation, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on inferring partner intent via theory of mind in agentic benchmarks.

card.one_liner: Evaluates LLMs' ability to induce belief states in others through planning and action rather than conversation.
card.key_idea: Introduces NCP-ExploreToM, a framework where agents achieve specific belief-state goals (true or false, 1st/2nd order) by manipulating objects and characters in simulated environments.
card.evaluation: Tested six frontier models (e.g., GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro) and humans across 600 task instances. GPT-5 succeeded on ~80% of tasks, outperforming humans.
card.limitation: Low ecological validity due to simple, arbitrary scenarios and non-agentic characters who are always compliant with directions.

slides.title: Metric Aggregation Divergence: A Hidden Validity Threat in Agent-Based Policy Optimization and a Contractual Remedy
slides.tldr: REMEDY FOR METRIC AGGREGATION DIVERGENCE IN ABM+MOEA
slides.highlight: This paper identifies metric aggregation divergence (MAD) in agent-based models coupled with multi-objective evolutionary algorithms, which can lead to incorrect policy recommendations. It is relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis of agent models.

card.one_liner: Metric Aggregation Divergence (MAD) causes silent policy recommendation errors when pipeline stages independently re-implement outcome metrics.
card.key_idea: MAD occurs when different pipeline stages use incommensurable aggregators (e.g., mean vs. entropy). The 'metric contract' remedy enforces a single shared callable across all stages.
card.evaluation: Tested via controlled experiments, three distinct ABMs, and audits of published toolboxes (EpidemiOptim, Lake Problem). Results show high champion disagreement (up to 83%).
card.limitation: Empirical validation is limited to two policy domains (ecology, epidemiology) and four ABM types; generalizability to other domains remains open.

slides.title: SICAGE: Speaker-Independent Culture-Aware Gesture Generation using TED4C-L Dataset
slides.highlight: SICAGE introduces a framework for generating culturally appropriate gestures that are independent of speaker identity. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and group norms in human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: SICAGE generates culture-aware gestures using speaker-independent embeddings to prevent confounding individual style with cultural patterns.
card.key_idea: A modular framework using Fishr regularization or adversarial learning to extract speaker-invariant cultural embeddings from audio/text, conditioning a real-time diffusion generator called ALaDiT.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the new TED4C-L dataset (106h, 4 cultures) using FGD, SRGR, BAS, and a user study; ALaDiT-FI outperformed MDM and DSG+ baselines.
card.limitation: The motion-based cultural classifier achieved only 45% accuracy, highlighting substantial intra-cultural variability that challenges gesture generation.

slides.title: Automatic Detection of Stress from Speech in the Trier Social Stress Test
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates the use of speaker diarization and acoustic-prosodic features to automatically detect human stress responses, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of team states.

card.one_liner: Speech-based machine learning can automatically distinguish stressful from non-stressful situations and predict certain stress responses.
card.key_idea: A pipeline using speaker diarization and ML models (XGBoost, SVR, RF) analyzed acoustic-prosodic features to classify TSST vs. f-TSST and predict cortisol and negative affect.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 50 participants using nested cross-validation. XGBoost achieved 82% accuracy; SVR and XGB outperformed mean baselines for cortisol and negative affect.
card.limitation: Could not consistently predict sAA reactivity or 20-minute post-task cortisol values.

slides.title: Parametric Skills
slides.tldr: CONVERTING TEXTUAL SKILLS INTO PARAMETERS FOR BETTER EXPLOITATION
slides.highlight: This framework converts textual skills into parameters via a hypernetwork to improve skill exploitation, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on skill acquisition and the transition from procedural instructions to proficient execution.

card.one_liner: ParametricSkills converts textual problem-solving skills into LoRA adapters via a hypernetwork for context-free exploitation.
card.key_idea: A hypernetwork is pretrained on a 45.8k skill library and fine-tuned on exploitation trajectories to map textual skills directly into parametric LoRA adapters.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on six SWE subtasks using Qwen3-8B; outperformed in-context learning by 6.44 points (DeepSeek-V4-Flash judge), with higher BERT and F1 scores.
card.limitation: Initial generated-skill LoRAs can underperform the base model if the quality of the initial textual skills is low.
